Title: Anwar: Every early vote a trust to strengthen welfare of security personnel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on security personnel casting their ballots early in the Negri Sembilan polls to continue supporting the coalition's candidates.
The prime minister said every vote cast would not only determine the direction of the state but also represent a mandate that his administration must uphold, particularly in safeguarding the welfare of security personnel and their families.
"With humility, I appeal to friends and family members from the armed forces and police who will carry out their responsibility as early voters to continue placing their trust in PH candidates.
"Every vote cast is not merely to determine the direction of the state, but is a trust that we must carry in order to further strengthen the welfare of security personnel and their families," he said in a social media post.
PH and Barisan Nasional (BN) formed the Negri Sembilan government following the 2023 state election after securing a combined 31 of the 36 seats.
PH won 17 seats and BN secured 14, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) won the remaining five.
Anwar acknowledged more needed to be done, saying he did not consider the government's efforts so far to be sufficient.
"However, with continued support and mandate, InsyaAllah, we will continue to work harder to uplift the nation's dignity, safeguard the welfare of the people and strengthen the well-being of all members of the security forces," he added.
Early voting
for the Negri Sembilan polls will take place on July 28, involving 16,884 military personnel and their spouses, as well as 5,455 police personnel.
Polling day is set for Aug 1.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nicky Liow not PKR member, says Fuziah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PKR has denied businessman Nicky Liow is a member of the party following his appearance at a party event two days ago.
Its secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh said a check of the party's records found no indication that Liow, whose full name is Liow Soon Hee, had joined PKR.
She said there was also no record of him submitting a membership application.
"I can confirm that Liow Soon Hee, also known as Nicky Liow, is not on the party's membership list.
"His name is also not on the list of those who have applied to become members," she said in a statements.
Questions over Liow's association with the party surfaced after a photograph showed him with PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at the event.
Liow was seen in the photograph wearing a PKR Youth shirt bearing the party logo.
Liow was charged at the Shah Alam Sessions Court in April 2022 with
26 counts of money laundering
involving RM36 million.
He had previously been on the run for about a year following a police crackdown on an alleged organised crime group linked to "Macau Scam" activities.
He was also charged in absentia with being a member of an organised crime group before later receiving a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sombre farewell for six friends killed in Bentong crash
Article:
TEMERLOH: A sombre atmosphere enveloped the cremation ceremonies as the remains of six friends who were tragically killed in an accident on Jalan Karak Lama in Bentong yesterday were cremated at two locations today.
The remains of V. Mugilan, 25; K. Dineshvaran, 22; and 17-year-old S.K. Kiisven were cremated at the Mentakab Hindu Crematorium, while K. Alaganathan, 21; A. Kanabati Raja, 19; and M. Paranthaman, 16, were laid to rest at the Sungai Kawang Crematorium in Karak, Bentong.
Earlier, friends and relatives gathered at the victims' respective homes to pay their final respects. Funeral prayers were also held before the hearses transported the remains to the two crematoriums.
At the Mentakab Hindu Crematorium, family members could not hold back tears as they gathered around the coffins before they were moved into the high-temperature chambers.
Hundreds of people present at the crematorium struggled to contain their emotions, and none were prepared to speak to members of the media. The cremation ceremony began at about 3pm.
In the incident, the six friends were travelling in a Toyota Camry when the vehicle is believed to have lost control on a hilly and winding stretch near Kampung Jambu Rias before crashing into an oncoming lorry.
All
six occupants were killed
on the spot, while the lorry driver sustained serious injuries.
Meanwhile, Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail conveyed his condolences to the families of the six friends, describing the tragedy as heart-wrenching and a profound loss to their loved ones and all those who knew them.
"It is with deep sorrow that I extend my condolences to the families of the six friends who died in the road accident.
"On behalf of the Pahang government, I extend my deepest sympathies to all family members who are going through an incredibly difficult time. May the families be granted the strength and patience to face this immense trial," he wrote on Facebook.
It was reported that the group had earlier attended a
prayer ceremony
with their families at the Sungai Kawang Estate temple before heading out for a meal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Ayob Khan calls for review of top police leadership structure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Retiring Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay has proposed a review and realignment of the police's top leadership structure, saying it should better reflect the responsibilities and workload carried by the force.
He said the proposal was not motivated by his impending retirement, noting that he had raised the matter publicly with Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail about two months ago during a Wira Madani programme in Kuantan.
He said the structure needs to be corrected and reorganised because there were some inconsistencies and irregularities.
"If you look at it, the Inspector-General of Police is graded Turus 2, while the Deputy Inspector-General of Police is JUSA A.
"The deputy should be graded Turus 3, followed by department directors at JUSA A and state police chiefs at JUSA B.
"That would be more appropriate and aligned," he told reporters after the Deputy Inspector-General of Police handover ceremony at the Police Training Centre (Pulapol) today.
Under Malaysia's public service grading system, Turus grades are reserved for the government's highest-ranking management positions, while JUSA (Jawatan Utama Sektor Awam) grades are senior executive appointments below the Turus level.
Ayob also said the police leadership structure should not be compared with that of the armed forces, as both organisations have distinct functions and operational requirements.
"The military has three services. It doesn't mean that because they have three JUSA A positions, we should only have three as well. We have 10 departments.
"Our workload continues to increase with population growth, and we need more investigating officers. There has to be a difference," he said.
He stressed that the proposal was not made for his personal benefit as he was retiring, but to ensure the welfare and career progression of future police officers continued to receive the government's attention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No Malaysians reported involved in Berlin attack - Embassy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: No Malaysians have been reported to be involved in an attack during the Christopher Street Day celebrations in Berlin, Germany, on Saturday night.
This was confirmed by the Malaysian Embassy in Berlin on Sunday.
The embassy also extended its sympathies to those who were affected by the tragedy, which left one person dead and at least 16 others injured.
"Our thoughts and prayers are with the victims, their families and everyone affected by this tragedy," read the statement posted on its official Facebook page.
The embassy said it was monitoring the aftermath of the incident, adding that any Malaysians requiring consular assistance or further information may contact the embassy via email at mwberlin@kln.gov.my or by telephone at +49 (0)30 885749-0.
According to the German Press Agency (dpa), a vehicle drove into a crowd in Berlin's Tiergarten area shortly after 10pm (local time) on Saturday (July 25), prompting organisers to call off the Christopher Street Day event.
One woman was killed, and 16 others were injured, including three who sustained life-threatening injuries and eight who were seriously hurt, while
police
launched a search for the suspect.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pavilion Reit set for higher rents after Parkson space revamp
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pavilion Real Estate Investment Trust (Reit) is expected to secure a significant rental uplift at Pavilion KL by November as new tenants move into space vacated by an anchor tenant, Kenanga Research said.
Anchor tenant Parkson has surrendered 68,000 sq ft of retail space, which will be reconfigured to accommodate 37 new tenants.
The reconfiguration temporarily reduced Pavilion KL's occupancy rate to 91 per cent from 97 per cent.
"We believe Pavilion Reit will likely secure significant rental uplift from the incoming tenants by November, given the low rental base previously enjoyed by the anchor tenant.
"More importantly, this strategic reconfiguration should enhance the mall's appeal by introducing new offerings that cater to current market trends, potentially attracting higher foot traffic," the research house said in a note.
Kenanga Research raised its financial year 2027 (FY27) earnings forecast by four per cent, citing the tenant reconfiguration exercise and lower electricity costs following the group's new tariff structure with Tenaga Nasional Bhd.
It said Pavilion Reit's first-half net profit came in within expectations, accounting for 47 per cent of its full-year forecast and 49 per cent of the consensus estimate.
The group also declared a gross dividend of 5.17 sen, keeping it on track to meet Kenanga Research's FY26 dividend forecast of 11.3 sen.
For the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, Pavilion Reit's net profit rose to RM89.03 million from RM78.66 million a year earlier. Revenue increased four per cent to RM221.01 million from RM213.34 million previously.
Kenanga Research maintained its "Outperform" call on the Reit with a target price of RM1.95.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mohamad: BN policies ensured aid for Negri Sembilan's vulnerable
Article:
REMBAU: REMBAU: The social safety net introduced during Barisan Nasional's administration in Negri Sembilan was aimed at ensuring no citizen was left behind during tough times, says Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
The Negri Sembilan BN chairman said the policy was among his priorities when he served as menteri besar to ensure residents received immediate government aid when facing hardships.
"My policy when leading Negri Sembilan back then was first and foremost the social safety net policy.
"I wanted the people of Negri Sembilan to feel secure and know that if anything happened to them, the government was there to help so that no one was left behind," he said at an event with the Indian community in Taman Intan, Rantau, last night.
Mohamad said his experience growing up in hardship following his father's death drove him to establish the policy so other children would not suffer a similar fate.
"I do not want children going to sleep crying from hunger. I have been through that. My father passed away, and being an orphan back then was difficult.
"I introduced this policy because I do not want any child to go through what I experienced," he said.
He said the policy helped poor families, low-income households, and orphans receive the support and protection they needed.
In his speech, Mohamad also highlighted the housing policy implemented during his tenure to ensure every resident had proper shelter.
"I do not want anyone in Negri Sembilan going to sleep with only the moon and stars above them, meaning they have no roof over their heads.
"We built homes for the needy so every resident in Negri Sembilan has a place that protects them from the rain and heat," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ayob Khan:  I wanted banking career, but friend persuaded me to join police
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Outgoing Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay today revealed that he never intended to join the police force, saying his original ambition after university was to pursue a career in banking.
Speaking at his farewell and handover ceremony at the Police Training Centre (Pulapol), Ayob said he was working for a private company after graduating from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia in 1990 when a friend persuaded him to attend a police recruitment interview.
"I never had any intention of joining the police and was not interested in becoming a police officer.
"My focus was to become a bank officer," he said in his farewell speech here today.
Ayob said he was initially informed that he had only been placed on the reserve list after the interview, but was unexpectedly called up about three months later.
"I joined the police without any connections. It was simply my rezeki (providence)," he said.
He reported for duty in 1991 and underwent training as a police cadet before beginning his career in the Special Branch, where he spent much of his service before rising through the ranks.
Ayob said his years in the intelligence division laid the foundation for a career that later saw him hold several key appointments, including Johor police chief, before being appointed to Bukit Aman and eventually becoming Deputy Inspector-General of Police.
Reflecting on his journey, he said Muslims should always believe that sustenance and opportunities were determined by God, rather than by people.
"People can make plans, but ultimately Allah determines the outcome. Never be afraid that your sustenance will be taken away," he said.
Ayob said this belief eventually led him to shoulder the responsibility of becoming the nation's Deputy Inspector-General of Police, a position he had never imagined holding during his nearly 35 years in the force.
Earlier, Ayob officially handed over his duties to Special Branch director Datuk Seri Ibrahim Darus, who assumes the role of acting Deputy Inspector-General of Police.
The ceremony was witnessed by Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bella, Syed Saddiq spark wedding buzz with bridal-inspired photos
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bella Astillah and Syed Saddiq Abdul Rahman have sparked social media speculation after sharing photographs in wedding-inspired attire, which netizens described as a pre-wedding shoot.
The photos and videos, posted on their Instagram accounts with the caption "Love story from KL to London", appear to be part of a collaboration with a fashion boutique.
"Every girl deserves her fairytale moment. Okay, I'm officially obsessed with the 'Fleurie'. It's so flowy, so pretty and honestly giving main princess energy," the post read.
The comments section was flooded with well-wishes from fans, many of whom expressed hope that preparations for the couple's wedding would proceed smoothly.
"This is the only fairytale I believe in because this one is really going to come true," one user commented.
"Looks like the date is getting closer," another wrote.
"So beautiful. I can't take my eyes off them," another social media user said.
Speculation over their wedding date has circulated in recent weeks, particularly after the
couple visited the office
of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad in Putrajaya.
Although the purpose of the visit was not disclosed, observers speculated they were delivering a wedding invitation for an upcoming ceremony.
Some netizens have also speculated that the couple may have chosen Aug 8, which falls on the date combination 8.8.26, as their wedding day.
Previously, Syed Saddiq reportedly confirmed to the media that both families had
agreed on a wedding date,
though it was not ready to be announced publicly.
He was also reported as saying that the wedding could take place earlier than originally planned, rather than towards the end of the year.
Bella Astillah and Syed Saddiq announced their engagement on March 28.
Bella was previously married to Singaporean singer and actor Aliff Aziz in 2016.
The couple divorced in 2019, reconciled during the iddah period, and divorced a second time on June 13, 2024.
They have two children together: Mohamad Ayden Adrean, 9, and Ara Adreanna, 6.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ayob Khan: Integrity must start from the top, no room for police misconduct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Retiring Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay today warned that misconduct within the police force would become entrenched if personnel involved in criminal activities were protected instead of being brought to justice..
Responding to questions on the recent arrests of personnel, including 12 policemen accused of extorting RM2 million from a Chinese national, Ayob said the force must take a zero-tolerance approach regardless of rank.
"We have to be firm. If we are not firm and continue protecting such activities, this is what will happen.
"Do not allow it to become a culture. If something is wrong, take action. Do not look at the person's rank," he said after his farewell ceremony at the Police Training Centre (Pulapol) today.
Drawing from his own experience, Ayob said he had never hesitated to act against errant policemen during his tenure, including arresting senior personnel suspected of wrongdoing.
"When I headed the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department, I arrested a superintendent. During investigations linked to Nicky Liow, I also arrested an assistant commissioner. Some officers were arrested while others faced disciplinary action.
"There must never be any cover-up. If we cover up the involvement of police officers in criminal activities, it will eventually become part of the culture. If corruption is accepted as a culture, then we are finished," he said.
Ayob said integrity must be demonstrated from the highest levels of leadership, saying strong leadership would set the tone for the rest of the organisation.
"It must start from the top. If those at the top are firm, those below will follow. I'm speaking in a broader context, not just about the Inspector-General of Police or Deputy IGP.
"The country's top leadership must also uphold integrity. If those at the top are not right, how can those below be right?" he said.
The 59-year-old said his stance had remained unchanged throughout his career, describing himself as an enforcement officer committed to facts and the rule of law rather than popularity.
"I've always said the same thing. Many people may not like me because I speak firmly and do not compromise. If you want to lead, you have to be firm."
Ayob officially retired today after nearly 35 years of service in the police force.
He consistently championed integrity, accountability and decisive action against corruption and abuse of power throughout his career.
It was reported that
12 policemen
of various ranks have been arrested for allegedly extorting RM2 million from a Chinese national.
Sources said the victim was released after paying US$140,000 (about RM560,000) to the suspects.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast in parts of Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several states across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak until 6pm today.
The affected areas are Langkawi in Kedah; Kinta, Perak Tengah, Kampar, Hilir Perak, Batang Padang and Muallim in Perak; Tumpat, Pasir Mas, Kota Bharu, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Bachok, Machang, Pasir Puteh and Kuala Krai in Kelantan; and Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus and Kemaman in Terengganu.
In Pahang, the warning covers Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Bentong, Temerloh, Kuantan, Bera, Pekan and Rompin, as well as Hulu Selangor and Gombak in Selangor.
It also affects Jempol and Tampin in Negeri Sembilan, and Tangkak, Segamat, Kluang, Mersing and Kota Tinggi in Johor.
In Sabah, the affected areas are Sipitang, Tenom, Beaufort, Keningau and Tambunan in the Interior; Papar, Putatan, Penampang, Kota Kinabalu and Tuaran on the West Coast; Lahad Datu in Tawau; and Kinabatangan in Sandakan.
In Sarawak, the warning covers Tatau and Sebauh in Bintulu, Subis in Miri, as well as Limbang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Integrity is the police force's greatest asset, says Ayob Khan in farewell message
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Retiring Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay left the police force with a simple but powerful message: never compromise on integrity, regardless of the circumstances.
In his farewell address after more than 34 years of service, Ayob reminded officers and personnel that character was the greatest asset a police officer could possess, warning that authority and rank were merely trusts that would ultimately be accounted for before God.
Quoting a well-known saying, he told the gathering: "If you lose your money, you lose nothing. If you lose your house, you lose something. If you lose your character, you lose everything."
"Every trust will be questioned. Every authority will be accounted for. In the end, we will all stand before Allah not with our ranks or positions, but with our deeds," he said.
Ayob also urged police officers to remain steadfast in doing what was right, even when it was difficult, unpopular or came with personal consequences.
He said courage was not the absence of fear, but the willingness to stand up for what was right despite the price that might have to be paid.
"The law cannot choose who should face action. Justice cannot bow to rank, position, race, religion or influence," he said.
Reflecting on his career, Ayob said some of his decisions were welcomed while others were misunderstood, but he had always believed police officers must prioritise doing what was right over what was easy.
He also called on the force to continue engaging professionally with the media while ensuring officers who carried out their duties properly were defended.
At the same time, he stressed that those who committed offences must face action without fear or favour.
"We want the Royal Malaysia Police to continue being respected. We want officers and personnel to be protected when they carry out their duties properly. We also want those who commit wrongdoing to face action without favouritism, while safeguarding the trust placed in us by the people," he said.
In one of the strongest messages of his farewell speech, Ayob warned officers never to abuse the authority entrusted to them or allow personal interests to tarnish the reputation of the police force.
"Do not destroy this force for personal gain. Do not sell your dignity for money. Do not use your authority to oppress the weak, and never forget that behind every power we hold are people who expect justice.
"Hold firmly to the integrity that we wear on our chest. It is not about who we are when people are watching, but who we are when no one is looking," he said.
Ayob, who officially retired today after serving as the 29th Deputy Inspector-General of Police, also urged officers to safeguard the honour of the institution built through the sacrifices of generations of police personnel.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail described Ayob as a leader synonymous with commitment, firmness and integrity, saying he had consistently upheld the rule of law throughout his career.
Khalid said Ayob's unwavering stance against militancy and commitment to preserving integrity should serve as an example for future generations of police leaders.
He also described Ayob as more than just his deputy, but a trusted partner who stood firmly beside him in steering the police force through numerous challenges while upholding the honour of the "Sang Saka Biru".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar extends condolences to families of Bentong crash victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the families of six victims killed in a road accident along Jalan Karak Lama in Bentong, Pahang.
In a post on X today, Anwar said he and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, were deeply saddened by the tragedy.
"My condolences to all the victims' family members. May they be granted strength and fortitude, and may those injured be blessed with a speedy recovery.
"This tragedy serves as a reminder to all of us that road safety must never be taken lightly," he said.
In the 4am incident yesterday, six men died at the scene after their car in collided with a one-tonne lorry on Jalan Karak Lama heading towards Temerloh, near Klinik Desa Jambu Rias in Bentong.
Those killed were the car driver, V. Mugilan, 25, and passengers K. Dineshvaran, 22, K. Alaganathan, 21, A. Kanabati Raja, 19, S. Kiisven, 17, and M. Paranthaman, 16. The 31-year-old lorry driver sustained serious injuries.
Preliminary police investigations found that the car, travelling from Kuantan to Kuala Lumpur, was believed to have veered into the opposite lane while descending a hill before colliding with the lorry. - Bernama
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rantau Panjang celebrates Aliff's historic ONE Championship triumph
Article:
RANTAU PANJANG: Kelantanese, especially residents of Rantau Panjang, are celebrating hometown hero Ahmad Nor Iman Aliff Rakib's remarkable achievement after he won the ONE Championship interim strawweight Muay Thai world title in Bangkok on Friday.
The Kelantan-born fighter stunned Thai legend Sam-A Gaiyanghadao with a fifth-round stoppage at Lumpinee Stadium, capping years of sacrifice and dedication to become Malaysia's latest world champion.
Taman Bakti Residents' Association chairman Nik Mohamad Mustapa said the community was immensely proud that one of its own had brought glory to Kelantan and Malaysia.
"We are extremely proud of Aliff's achievement. He has made Malaysia and Rantau Panjang famous on the world stage.
"We are planning to organise a special welcome-home celebration for him so residents can congratulate him personally on his historic success," he said when met today.
He said sporting excellence runs in the family, with Aliff's elder brother, Ahmad Nor Iman Hakim, having won a gold medal for Malaysia at the 2023 SEA Games in Vietnam.
Villager Che Mazahar Che Mat, 52, who has known Aliff's father for many years, described the victory as an emotional moment for the people of Rantau Panjang.
"We were thrilled watching the fight. It gave me goosebumps seeing his kicks and punches.
"When he defeated such an experienced opponent, we felt incredibly proud because he had raised Malaysia's name on the international stage," he said.
Aliff's father, former Malaysian boxer Rakib Ahmad, 52, said the title was the result of years of perseverance and sacrifice.
"I am grateful and proud because all his hard work since childhood has finally paid off for Malaysia.
"He started training when he was only five or six years old. At the age of 14, he moved to Bangkok to continue training and worked hard on his own to pursue his dream.
"As the fight progressed, I could see he had a good chance of winning despite facing such an accomplished opponent," said Rakib, a father of four.
Rakib said Aliff, his second child, had remained focused on his ambition despite the challenges of living and training away from home at a young age.
"He never gave up. This world title is proof that dedication, discipline and sacrifice can turn dreams into reality," he said.
Aliff sealed the historic victory one minute and nine seconds into the fifth and final round, becoming the first Malaysian to win an interim ONE Championship world title.
The 22-year-old also pocketed a US$50,000 performance bonus, capping a landmark night for Malaysian Muay Thai.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno must win urban seats to regain relevance, says Johari
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must formulate a new strategy to regain support from urban voters after losing 10 of the 11 parliamentary seats in Kuala Lumpur, party vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said.
Johari said Malaysia's changing demographic landscape, with a majority of the population now living in urban areas, required Umno to adapt its approach and strengthen its appeal among city voters.
The Titiwangsa member of parliament said that while he managed to retain his seat, it was not enough as Barisan Nasional only controls one parliamentary seat in the capital.
"We are a society that is increasingly urban. Although I won, I consider it a loss. Why? Because Kuala Lumpur has 11 parliamentary seats.
"Ten parliamentary seats were won by other parties. Yet it was Umno and BN that developed Kuala Lumpur.
"The construction of People's Housing Programme (PPR) homes and public housing was also carried out by BN.
"But we lost. That is why I always believe that if not many Umno leaders win in Kuala Lumpur, we are still losing," he said when opening the Titiwangsa Umno division delegates meeting at the World Trade Centre (WTC) today.
Johari said Umno's strength in the past was largely built on support from rural voters, where the majority of Malays and Bumiputera communities lived.
However, he said migration to cities had changed the country's political landscape and voter patterns.
"The Malay community living in cities used to be very small. Those who dominated urban areas were mainly non-Malays, particularly the Chinese community.
"Today, Malays have also moved into urban areas. If we want to strengthen Umno and maintain its role as the anchor party within BN, Umno must win urban seats."
Johari acknowledged that winning urban constituencies would not be easy, but said it was essential for Umno's future survival.
"If we want to improve Umno and ensure it remains the anchor in BN, we must win all urban seats. But winning urban seats is not an easy task."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Knives, scissors thrown from apartment pierce restaurant canopy, nearly miss customers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Customers at a seafood restaurant in Pandan Indah had a close shave when knives and scissors thrown from an apartment building landed near them while they were having dinner last Tuesday.
The 47-year-old restaurant owner, who only wanted to be known as Chia, said the incident happened about 7.20pm.
"I was shocked when I heard customers screaming while they were eating. After checking, I saw a pair of scissors had pierced through the canopy.
"A customer was eating close to where the scissors landed, but fortunately, no one was injured.
"Besides the scissors, about five or six knives were also thrown from the apartment building and found near the lake beside my restaurant. I then informed the apartment management before lodging a police report," he said.
He said the management also informed him that the individual responsible for the act had been arrested.
"Previously, foreign workers from the apartment would often throw rubbish down, but this is the first time knives and scissors have been thrown down like this," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police hunting for Berlin Pride attacker
Article:
BERLIN: Berlin police have published a picture of a 21-year-old man suspected of carrying out Saturday night's attack at the Pride celebration, in which a vehicle rammed into a crowd, killing one person and injuring more than a dozen others.
In an online post on Sunday, police urged members of the public to help them find the man, identified as Abdul B, adding that it was not clear whether he acted alone.
They said more than one person may have got out of the vehicle after it came to a halt near the city's Brandenburg Gate.
Three of the 16 people injured in the attack were in a life-threatening condition, and some of the injuries included stab wounds, police and emergency services said.
Organisers of the annual Christopher Street Day celebrations, Berlin's annual LGBTQ Pride event, cancelled the remaining events.
[[nid:1497403]]
SUSPECTED PERPETRATOR
Police described the wanted man as slim, about 1.90 metres (6ft 2in) tall, with black hair, and last seen wearing a black hooded top and white trousers.
They said he was part of the "Islamist spectrum".
"Who can share anything about his current whereabouts?" the statement said.
Several key details about the incident remain unclear.
While police described the white vehicle only vaguely as possibly a car, minivan or minibus, tabloid newspaper Bild reported that it was a white Citroen SpaceTourer van rented by Abdul B.
Police are also searching for a second suspected attacker, Bild reported.
Police said the vehicle came to a stop in the central Tiergarten park.
"According to our latest information, the vehicle drove ... into the Tiergarten around 10pm (2000 GMT), injuring several people in the process, and then came to a standstill after hitting a tree here in the Tiergarten," a police spokesperson at the scene said overnight.
"It was empty, which is why we are currently working intensively to track down the perpetrator or perpetrators."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK's Burnham would call out Trump if in Britain's interest, he tells BBC
Article:
BENGALURU: New UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham "will always put Britain's interests first", he told the BBC in an interview, parts of which were released on Sunday, when asked whether he was willing to call out US President Donald Trump.
Burnham's predecessor, Keir Starmer, who announced he was stepping down last month, had a fraught relationship with Trump, who criticised him over differences on the US-Israeli war on Iran, immigration, energy and technology regulation.
While Trump initially described Starmer's successor as "extremely liberal", he said this week he had a "very good conversation" with Burnham, who became Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade on Monday.
In his first major interview since taking office, BBC journalist Laura Kuenssberg asked Burnham if he was willing to call out Trump if he thought it was the right thing to do.
"All leaders have to do that. You have to defend your own national interest before anything else. That's what you're required to do if you're to do this job properly," he said.
The prime minister also said he would not call a general election before 2029.
"I'm going to rule it out. Yeah, there's no early general election. I don't think people want it," he said.
On Britain's national defence, Burnham said he was "absolutely committed" to what was promised to NATO partners.
"The first challenge facing us both is to ensure that the defence investment plan is fully funded, and that's the thing that's right in front of us, and we need to work that through as we go towards the budget later this year," he said.
Burnham's newly appointed chancellor, John Healey, resigned as defence minister in the previous government after saying that, unless a commitment was made to spend 3 per cent of GDP on defence by 2030, Britain would not be safe.
"We've got to work out the way of doing that," Burnham said when pressed on the 3 per cent of GDP commitment.
The full interview will air on the BBC's Panorama programme on Monday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: N9 polls: Fahmi calls for focus on policies, not 3R or slander
Article:
SEREMBAN: Pakatan Harapan (PH) has urged all parties contesting in the Negri Sembilan election to conduct mature campaigns by presenting ideas, policies and track records, rather than exploiting race, religion and royalty (3R) issues or spreading slander to win voters' support.
PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said elections are a democratic platform for the people to determine the state's future, and political competition should focus on solutions affecting the rakyat, including jobs, home ownership, the cost of living and economic development.
He said although the campaign entered its ninth day today, there were still individuals and parties exploiting racial sentiments and spreading slander to divert attention from real issues.
"Political parties should compete through ideas, policies, track records and solutions to the people's problems, not by resorting to politics of hatred.
"When a party runs out of ideas, it sells hatred. But a party that is confident in its track record and offerings presents hope. PH has chosen to offer hope, not hatred," he said at a press conference at the Negri Sembilan PH main operations room here today.
Fahmi also called on all parties to respect election laws and ensure campaigning is conducted in a mature, responsible and fact-based manner.
He said Negri Sembilan has long been known as a peaceful and harmonious state, and its unity should not be undermined for political gain.
Fahmi said PH would continue to champion moderate, inclusive and constructive politics by emphasising leadership that works for and unites the people regardless of race, religion or background.
Asked about the involvement of celebrity Caprice in the PH campaign, Fahmi said Caprice is not an official influencer representing the coalition in the state election.
Early voting
is on July 28, while polling is on Aug 1.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trader fined RM700 for selling contaminated sushi at Ramadan bazaar [WATCH]
Article:
SETIU: A trader was fined RM700 by the magistrate's court here today after pleading guilty to selling sushi contaminated with harmful bacteria at a Ramadan bazaar.
Khairul Fazlan Ab Aziz, 33, entered his plea after the charge was read before magistrate Iffah Nabihah Mohd Ishak.
The court ordered him to serve a one-month jail sentence if he fails to pay the fine.
Khairul Fazlan was charged with selling ready-to-eat 'Sushi Miniroll Chicken Floss' contaminated with pathogenic microorganisms to an authorised officer at the Sungai Tarom Ramadan Bazaar in Bandar Permaisuri, Setiu, at 4.50pm on Feb 22.
Laboratory analysis revealed the food contained Staphylococcus aureus bacteria at a level of 5.5 x 10² CFU/g, rendering it contaminated under Regulation 39(2) of the Food Regulations 1985.
The offence carries a maximum fine of RM10,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both upon conviction.
Prosecuting officer Nik Muhammad Hanif Nik Abdull Halim urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence, stating that enforcement action is vital to ensure food sold to the public meets safety standards and does not pose health risks.
The accused was unrepresented.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man arrested for repeatedly stealing money from mosque donation boxes
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH: A man believed to have repeatedly stolen money from donation boxes at Masjid Bandar Baru Sungai Buloh (MBBSB) here was finally arrested yesterday.
MBBSB manager Muhammad Faaez Khesim said police arrived just minutes after a report was lodged and detained the suspect.
He said the suspect was believed to have stolen money from MBBSB donation boxes several times and was also linked to similar incidents in the area.
"The mosque authorities have been working with the police as we had been monitoring this suspect for quite some time because he repeatedly carried out the same act.
"At MBBSB alone, we detected three cases where he stole money from donation boxes located along the corridor.
"We had already identified the suspect's vehicle. The first time he entered, he broke the donation box until it was damaged.
"Now, only one donation box remains because it is quite heavy for us to move it into the locked prayer hall," he said when contacted today.
He said the suspect targeted donation boxes along the mosque's corridor by using a wire to "fish" for money and would usually sneak in between 12.30am and 3am.
Faaez said the same suspect was believed to have stolen from the mosque twice within a few days earlier this month.
He said after identifying the suspect's modus operandi, the mosque authorities worked with the police to monitor his movements through closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage.
"After he broke in twice, we worked with the Sungai Buloh police station. The first and second incidents occurred only a few days apart, followed by a week when he was not seen.
"We were informed that the suspect was also believed to have stolen from other mosques during that period.
"However, during the third incident, as soon as I noticed suspicious movements, I contacted the police and informed the officer-in-charge of the station.
"It took no more than a few minutes, I think around two to three minutes, for them (police) to arrive and detain the man," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: N9 polls: Cops open 14 election offence investigation papers as of Saturday
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police have opened 14 investigation papers into election-related offences during the campaign period for the 16th Negri Sembilan state election as of yesterday, said state police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad.
He said three investigation papers were opened yesterday under Section 435 of the Penal Code for committing mischief by fire, causing loss of or damage to property.
Another two investigation papers were opened under Section 427 of the Penal Code for committing mischief resulting in loss of or damage to property.
He said the cases opened yesterday involved two police reports in Gemas, Tampin, concerning incidents of party flags being set on fire and campaign banners being vandalised, while one report in Titi, Jelebu involved a billboard that had been torn and damaged.
"Cumulatively, from July 18 to 25, the Negri Sembilan Police Contingent received 28 reports related to election offences," he said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, he said 94 of the 95 permit applications received yesterday for political ceramah and campaign activities were approved, bringing the total number of permits approved to 416.
Alzafny said police would continue to strengthen their level of preparedness, monitoring and enforcement throughout the campaign period, with firm action to be taken against any breach of the law.
"The public is urged to continue complying with the law, respect the democratic process and cooperate with the police to ensure the election is conducted in a peaceful, orderly and harmonious manner," he said.
Early voting for the Negri Sembilan state election has been set for Tuesday, while polling day is on Aug 1.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Probe into fake UNHCR cards, possible syndicate link in Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BARU: Kelantan Immigration Department is probing suspected fake UNHCR cards found on three Rohingya men, amid efforts to determine whether the documents were linked to any syndicate.
Its director, Garry Belayong John Siki, said the cases were the first involving suspected fake United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards detected by the department this year.
He said investigations into the documents were ongoing, including efforts to identify the source of the suspected forged cards and whether they were connected to a wider syndicate.
Garry said the three Rohingya men were among 20 foreigners detained during Op Mega, a joint enforcement operation carried out in Kota Baru on Friday.
"Of the 20 detained, only 10 have been remanded to facilitate investigations.
"Once investigations are completed, the investigation papers will be submitted to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for a decision on whether to press charges," he said.
Garry said the suspected fake UNHCR cards were seized from the three Rohingya men during the operation, involving the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Kota Baru Municipal Council-Islamic City.
He said the cards were confiscated after checks revealed discrepancies between the information in the documents and the physical appearance of the holders.
During the operation, 362 foreigners, including those from Myanmar, Nepal, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Indonesia and Thailand, were inspected.
Of those inspected, 20 foreign men aged between 30 and 60 were detained for various offences under the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the Immigration Regulations 1963.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN-PH deal not a lifelong contract, says Khaled
Article:
PORT DICKSON: The agreement between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Pakatan Harapan (PH) to form the federal government should not be regarded as permanently binding, Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
The Umno vice-president said the cooperation underpinning the unity government was forged to facilitate the formation of the federal administration following the 15th general election.
"It is not a lifelong contract. It was an agreement to form the federal government and should not be seen as binding indefinitely.
"We understood that circumstances at the time required us to work together. We agreed to do so to ensure the country had a government," he said after attending the 'Kesejahteraan Warga ATM' programme at Sirusa Camp today.
Khaled, who is also defence minister, was responding to criticism levelled at BN during the Negri Sembilan election campaign, with some accusing the coalition of being "ungrateful".
The criticism stemmed from BN's decision to contest against PH and form an electoral pact with Perikatan Nasional in the state election, despite both coalitions remaining partners in the federal unity government.
Meanwhile, Khaled said BN's decision to contest any election, including against PH, was aimed at returning the mandate to the people and allowing voters to decide which party they trusted to govern.
"That is why political parties go back to the people and seek the people's mandate. Ultimately, it is the people who will decide," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: University student remanded over newborn's body found at rubbish disposal area
Article:
KUALA LANGAT: A university student has been remanded for four days to assist in the investigation into the discovery of a newborn baby's body in a hostel rubbish disposal area here.
Kuala Langat district police chief Superintendent Akmalrizal Mohd Radzi said the remand order, which runs from yesterday until Tuesday, was granted to facilitate investigations under Section 318 of the Penal Code for concealment of birth.
"The suspect, a student in her teens believed to be the baby's mother, has been remanded for four days to assist in further investigations," he said in a statement today.
Police received a report from a man around midnight on Thursday regarding the discovery of the baby's body wrapped in cloth at the hostel's rubbish site.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN-PN pact in Negri polls not a template for other states, says Sharkar
Article:
KUANTAN: An Umno Supreme Council member has said electoral strategies adopted in one state should not automatically be applied elsewhere, as each state has its own political dynamics.
Datuk Seri Mohd Sharkar Shamsudin said the electoral understanding between Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional for the Negri Sembilan election should not be viewed as a template for polls in other states such as Selangor, Pahang and Melaka.
"What happened in the Negri Sembilan election does not necessarily apply to other states. The people of Negri Sembilan know what works best for their state, and it is not necessarily applicable elsewhere.
"That is why Malaysians must understand that the federal and state governments are two separate entities.
"There is nothing unusual about political arrangements differing between the two levels of government," he told reporters after opening the Indera Mahkota Umno division delegates' meeting today.
Citing Sabah as an example, Sharkar said DAP and PKR, which are part of the ruling coalition at the federal level, serve as opposition parties in the state, adding that there was nothing wrong with differing political alignments.
He urged the public not to take a narrow view of political developments, but to remain open-minded and consider the broader picture.
"It was different in the past when Umno controlled both the federal and state governments.
"Today, there are around 10 Malay-based political parties," he said.
BN and PN have reached an informal electoral understanding for the Negri Sembilan election, with BN contesting 25 seats and the Pas-led PN contesting the remaining 11.
On July 22, Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man was quoted as saying that a political understanding between BN and PN would enable the two coalitions to jointly control almost all states in Peninsular Malaysia.
Meanwhile, commenting on Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's statement, Sharkar said it was not surprising, describing it as typical of Sanusi's political style.
"Everyone knows that is how Sanusi is. If such remarks did not come from him, that would be more surprising. For me, it is just another statement from Sanusi.
"From my perspective, the statement may have been hurtful. Such remarks may affect people's feelings, but that does not necessarily mean they will influence voting decisions on polling day," he said.
During a ceramah in Negri Sembilan, Sanusi said Malaysia was the only Tanah Melayu for Malays, while other races had countries of origin such as India and China.
He later claimed that some quarters had manipulated his remarks for political gain.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Ibrahim assumes duties as acting deputy IGP as Ayob Khan bows out
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay retired today after nearly 35 years of service in the police force, ending a distinguished career that saw him lead some of Malaysia's most significant counter-terrorism and criminal investigations.
Datuk Seri Ibrahim Darus, the Bukit Aman Special Branch director, has assumed duties as acting Deputy Inspector-General of Police with immediate effect following Ayob Khan's mandatory retirement.
The handing-over ceremony was witnessed by Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail at the Police Training Centre here today.
Ayob Khan was appointed Deputy Inspector-General of Police on June 23, 2023, succeeding Tan Sri Razarudin Husain, who was subsequently elevated to the post of Inspector-General of Police.
Born on July 27, 1966, in Kota Setar, Kedah, Ayob Khan holds a Master's degree in Information Technology from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia.
He joined the police force in 1991 and began his policing career in 1993 with the Bukit Aman Special Branch as an Assistant Superintendent of Police, serving in the intelligence division for 15 years until attaining the rank of Assistant Commissioner of Police.
Ayob Khan rose to national prominence during his tenure with the Bukit Aman Special Branch's Counter-Terrorism Division (E8) between 2013 and 2019, where he led numerous operations that foiled militant attack plots and investigated high-profile terrorism cases involving the Islamic State (IS) militant group and the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam.
In 2020, he was appointed Johor police chief before returning to Bukit Aman in 2022 as Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director.
He was later appointed director of the Criminal Investigation Department before assuming the country's second-highest policing post in 2023.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aminuddin challenges opposition to prove PH left development agenda unfinished
Article:
PORT DICKSON: Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has hit back at opposition leaders claiming they want to resume an unfinished development agenda under the Pakatan Harapan state administration.
The Negri Sembilan PH chairman challenged his rivals to present factual evidence of any project or plan that had allegedly stalled during PH's five-year tenure leading the state.
"What has been stalled? If they are merely copy-pasting what PH has already implemented, it means those initiatives have already been carried out.
"They can talk about an unfinished agenda, but what exactly is it? Prove it and put it in writing. Until today, they have failed to show anything that was left behind," he said after a house-to-house walkabout in Bandar Baru Sunggala today.
He was responding to Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who denied that BN was copying PH's manifesto, claiming instead that BN sought to continue a development agenda that had been interrupted.
Meanwhile, Aminuddin described the political dynamics between BN and Perikatan Nasional as a political drama designed to confuse voters for political gain.
"Everyone knows they appear to have no common ground, yet at the same time, they met frequently and worked together, which ultimately resulted in 11 seats being allocated for PN to contest," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: German police hunt suspect after deadly car ramming near Berlin Gay Pride
Article:
BERLIN: German police searched on Sunday for a suspect believed linked to Islamist circles after a car ploughed into a crowd near Berlin's Gay Pride celebrations, killing one person and wounding 16 others.
The incident shattered what had been a day of celebration for hundreds of thousands attending Christopher Street Day, one of Europe's largest Pride events, and left revellers fleeing a central Berlin park as sirens echoed through the night.
Police told AFP the suspected vehicle was later found abandoned a few hundred metres from the heart of the festivities in Tiergarten park.
A manhunt involving helicopters and officers from several German states was under way across the capital on Sunday.
A suspect, believed to have links to "Islamist circles" had been "identified" but not yet arrested, police spokesman Florian Nath said.
An eyewitness near the main Pride stage at Brandenburg Gate told AFP that celebrations abruptly ended when police instructed people to leave.
"Go home, please," officers told participants as the crowd streamed away from the park, where emergency crews rushed to treat victims.
The attack occurred shortly before 10pm (2000 GMT) on Saturday.
"A vehicle entered the Tiergarten park and hit several people," police said.
One person died and 16 others were injured, including three with life-threatening injuries, according to Berlin fire department spokesman Dominik Pretz.
Around 30 more people were treated for shock at the scene.
Police spokesman Nath said investigators had identified a suspect but not yet made an arrest, adding that investigators believed he had links to "Islamist circles."
The search was widened to "the whole city" after the vehicle was discovered abandoned in the vast Tiergarten park.
The vehicle appeared to be "akin to a minivan or small SUV", Nath said.
The attack immediately revived memories of a series of deadly assaults that have shaken Germany in recent years and fuelled fierce debate over security.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed that those responsible would face justice.
In a statement, Merz described the incident as a "horrific act" and said he and Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt were being kept informed of developments.
Berlin Mayor Kai Wegner condemned what he called a brutal attack on "a gathering for a tolerant and peaceful Berlin."
Police had deployed more than 2,000 officers to secure the event.
Following the incident, additional personnel from across Germany joined the search operation, supported by helicopters equipped with thermal-imaging cameras.
An AFP journalist at the scene saw numerous emergency vehicles lining a nearby road and a large tent erected as police combed the area.
VIOLENT ATTACKS
Earlier Saturday, hundreds of thousands of people took part in the event, called Christopher Street Day in Germany, which is one of the biggest Pride events in Europe.
The march ended next to the Brandenburg Gate, which has been the venue for concerts since Friday.
Germany has in recent years seen several violent attacks at public spaces, including a stabbing in February 2025 at Berlin's Holocaust memorial, a stone's throw from the scene of Saturday's incident, in which a Spanish tourist was seriously injured.
A Syrian man named only as Wassim Al M. was jailed in March for 13 years for that attack, with the court finding he acted in the name of the so-called Islamic State group.
Last month Taleb Jawad al-Abdulmohsen, a 51-year-old Saudi psychiatrist, was sentenced to life in prison for killing six people and wounding more than 300.
He drove a rented SUV through a crowded Christmas market in 2024 in the easter city of Magdeburg.
Abdulmohsen was an anti-Islam activist and his testimony at his trial was sometimes incoherent and riddled with conspiracy theories and fringe far-right ideas.
The deadliest such attack in recent years was a truck rampage at a Berlin Christmas market in December 2016 that killed 12 people.
Saturday's incident came two months before voters in Berlin elect a new state assembly.
Polls indicate that the centre-right CDU, to which Merz and Wegner both belong, will face a stiff challenge from both the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) and the far-left Linke parties.
Wegner himself said earlier this month he would not run for re-election after months of criticism over his handling of a major blackout in January apparently caused by sabotage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Defence Ministry identifies asset procurements for G2G execution, says Khaled
Article:
PORT DICKSON: The Defence Ministry has identified several asset procurements to be carried out through government-to-government (G2G) arrangements.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the approach would enable Malaysia to secure competitive pricing while providing greater assurance of supply.
"In the past, we used open tenders where all companies could participate, whether they were original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), agents, or others.
"This time, however, we will carry out the procurement through G2G arrangements.
"Among its advantages, G2G procurement not only enables us to secure competitive pricing but also provides greater assurance of supply, as the commitments are backed by the governments with which we are dealing," he told reporters after attending the Kesejahteraan Warga ATM programme at Sirusa Camp here.
Khaled said two memoranda of understanding (MoUs) had been signed to facilitate G2G procurement — one with Turkiye and another with South Korea.
"Several countries, including Italy and France, have also proposed conducting procurement through G2G arrangements."
Khaled said several criteria were applied in selecting Malaysia's G2G partners for asset procurements.
"We want to ensure that the countries we engage with are trusted partners and are willing to transfer technology to Malaysia, helping us develop our domestic defence industry."
He said the most important consideration was that procurement specifications were determined by the respective armed services.
"What is most important is that the specifications are determined by our respective services — the Army, Navy and Air Force.
"It is not a case of the government purchasing equipment arbitrarily; rather, procurement is carried out in close consultation with the respective services that require the equipment."
Khaled said G2G procurement was also more transparent because it eliminated intermediaries, resulting in a clearer procurement process and more competitive pricing.
On Friday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had reduced the cost of acquiring Littoral Mission Ships (LMS) by
15 per cent
through direct G2G negotiations with Turkiye.
He said the G2G procurement approach eliminated reliance on intermediaries, whose commissions had previously inflated the cost of defence acquisitions.
Anwar said he personally raised the proposal with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, suggesting that negotiations be conducted directly between the two governments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM Anwar extends condolences to families of six killed in Bentong crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the families of the six victims who were killed in a road crash along Jalan Karak Lama in Bentong, Pahang, early yesterday.
In a post on X today, Anwar said he and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, were deeply saddened by the tragedy.
“My condolences to all the victims’ family members. May they be granted strength and fortitude, and may those injured be blessed with a speedy recovery.
“This tragedy serves as a reminder to all of us that road safety must never be taken lightly,” he said.
In the incident at about 4 am yesterday, six men died at the scene after the Toyota Vios they were travelling in was involved in a collision with a one-tonne lorry on Jalan Karak Lama heading towards Temerloh, near Klink Desa Jambu Rias in Bentong.
Those killed were the car driver, V. Mugilan, 25, and passengers K. Dineshvaran, 22, K. Alaganathan, 21, A. Kanabati Raja, 19, S. Kiisven, 17, and M. Paranthaman, 16, while the 31-year-old lorry driver sustained serious injuries.
Preliminary police investigations found that the victims’ car, which was travelling from Kuantan to Kuala Lumpur, was believed to have veered onto the opposite lane while descending a hill before colliding with the lorry. — Bernama

Title: Ayob Khan retires as deputy IGP today after 35 years in police force, Ibrahim now acting DIGP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 —  Outgoing Deputy Inspector-General of Police (DIGP) Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay today handed over his duties as he retires from the police force.
In a ceremony witnessed by Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail at the Police Training Centre (Pulapol), Ayob handed over his duties as deputy IGP to Bukit Aman’s Special Branch director Datuk Seri Ibrahim Darus.
As the most senior director in service in the police force currently, Ibrahim will be serving as the acting deputy IGP while also continuing to hold his current post.
Ayob Khan, who is retiring as he turns 66 tomorrow, has been the DIGP since his appointment about three years ago on June 23, 2023.
Born in Kota Setar, Kedah, Ayob Khan has a degree in information technology from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia.
Throughout his 35-year career, Ayob had held various positions before becoming the DIGP, including as head of Bukit Aman’s Special Branch’s counter-terrorism division, Johor police chief, Bukit Aman’s Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director, and Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department director.

Title: Typhoon Noul forces Malaysia Airlines to cancel flights to Shenzhen and Hong Kong
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Malaysia Airlines has cancelled several flights between Kuala Lumpur, Shenzhen and Hong Kong as Typhoon Noul brings severe weather to southern China, disrupting air travel across the region.
The airline said services scheduled for July 25 and 26 — MH522 (Kuala Lumpur–Shenzhen), MH523 (Shenzhen–Kuala Lumpur), MH078 (Kuala Lumpur–Hong Kong) and MH079 (Hong Kong–Kuala Lumpur) — were called off due to deteriorating conditions linked to the approaching typhoon. It added that operations remain under close review and further updates will be issued directly to affected passengers and on its website.
Travellers were advised to update their contact details via the My Booking portal or the Malaysia Airlines mobile app to ensure they receive notifications promptly. The carrier said passengers on the cancelled flights may request refunds or rebook their journeys on the same route at no extra charge within 30 days of their original travel date. Safety of passengers and crew remains the airline’s “top priority”.
Checks on AirAsia’s flight status page showed similar disruptions, with flight AK126 from Kuala Lumpur to Shenzhen cancelled on Sunday. Other services on the same route — AK122 and AK128 — were delayed, alongside AK138 to Hong Kong and AK112 to Guangzhou.
Typhoon Noul is forecast to make landfall between Hong Kong and Guangdong from late July 25 to early July 26, bringing torrential rain and strong winds. Chinese authorities have evacuated more than 20,000 residents in Guangdong ahead of the storm, according to state broadcaster CCTV.

Title: Senior police officers among 12 arrested in alleged RM2m extortion of Chinese national
Article:
PETALING JAYA, July 26 — Twelve Malaysian police officers, including senior-ranking personnel, have been arrested over allegations they extorted RM2 million from a Chinese national, who was allegedly forced to pay RM560,000 for his release,
Utusan Malaysia
reported.
Citing unnamed sources, the newspaper said the victim paid US$140,000 (RM572,000) before later lodging a police report at the Dang Wangi district police headquarters.
“He later came forward to lodge a report at the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters (IPD).
“Following that, it is understood that 12 police officers and personnel were arrested, including some holding the ranks of Deputy Superintendent (DSP), Assistant Superintendent (ASP), and other ranks,” the source was quoted as saying.
According to the report, the officers had allegedly demanded RM2 million from the man.
“However, the victim was only able to pay RM560,000 before deciding to lodge a police report.
“Police also recovered part of the money believed to be linked to the case,” the source added.
Dang Wangi district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sazalee Adam confirmed the arrests when contacted by
Utusan Malaysia
.
The report did not say when the alleged extortion took place or identify the officers involved.
It also did not state whether any of the suspects had been charged.

Title: DPM Zahid: No one above the law if implicated in Tabung Haji RCI report
Article:
TAMPIN, July 26 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has stressed that no one is above the law if their names are implicated in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said the RCI findings must be made known transparently, and if there are elements of wrongdoing, appropriate action can be taken according to due legal process.
“The findings from the RCI investigation and study must be made known transparently. If there is any abuse of power, irregularity, criminal breach of trust or other malpractices, there are processes to lodge police reports and conduct investigations in terms of commercial crimes and other legal aspects, which can be carried out subsequently,” he said
He said this when met by reporters at the Malaysian Armed Forces Southern Zone Family Day Carnival at Kem Syed Sirajuddin, Gemas, which was also attended by Army Chief Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman here today.
Asked whether the release of the report would affect BN’s campaign in the Negeri Sembilan state election, Ahmad Zahid, who is also UMNO president, said he did not think it would have an impact as people in the state are capable of making mature and wise assessments.
“I do not think it will have any influence… The people, especially voters in Negeri Sembilan, are very wise in making their assessments. In their minds and hearts, they know which candidate and which coalition they will vote for,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had earlier expressed confidence that the Cabinet would agree to the proposal to make the RCI report on TH public after it was tabled for Cabinet consideration.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, explained that the previous delay in releasing the report was because the government did not want confidence in TH to be affected.
However, he said the situation is now different as the institution has been strengthened and received international recognition.
Early voting for the Negeri Sembilan state election is scheduled for Tuesday, while polling day is on Aug 1.
For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman: Six to be charged over RM7m Petaling Jaya kidnapping tomorrow as two suspects become prosecution witnesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Six men will be charged tomorrow over the RM7 million ransom kidnapping in Petaling Jaya after police completed their investigation into the case, while two other suspects have been released to become prosecution witnesses.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Comm Datuk M. Kumar said in a statement that the investigation paper into the case, reported on July 17, was referred to the Attorney General’s Chambers on July 24, which subsequently directed that charges be brought against the six suspects.
They will be charged under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961 for kidnapping for ransom, an offence punishable upon conviction with between 30 and 40 years’ imprisonment and whipping.
The six are due to appear before the Petaling Jaya Sessions Court at 9.30am tomorrow.
Kumar said the remaining two suspects — a man and a woman — had been released and bound over under Section 118 of the Criminal Procedure Code to serve as prosecution witnesses.
The kidnapping occurred in Petaling Jaya on July 17, when a 46-year-old woman reported that her husband had been abducted and that the kidnappers were demanding RM7 million for his release.
Police rescued the victim less than 48 hours later during a special operation at a residential unit in I-City, Shah Alam, which also led to the arrests of the suspects.
At the time, Kumar said the operation was carried out by Bukit Aman CID with assistance from Bukit Aman Special Branch and the Selangor CID.
Police also seized various types of drugs, several mobile phones and a number of vehicles believed to have been used in the crime.

Title: Ahead of 60th anniversary, King’s royal diplomacy elevates Russia-Malaysia ties, says ambassador
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — The royal diplomacy of Malaysia’s King, Sultan Ibrahim, has brought the people of Russia and Malaysia closer despite the geographical distance between the two countries, while elevating bilateral ties to a new sphere, Russian Ambassador to Malaysia Naiyl Latypov said.
Praising His Majesty's royal approach, Latypov said the King's diplomacy has elevated Russia-Malaysia bilateral ties as the two countries prepare to mark the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations next year.
"Russia highly appreciates His Majesty’s royal diplomacy. Such warmth is something completely new in our relations. His Majesty's personal attitude towards Russia has enabled Russia-Malaysia bilateral ties to enter a new sphere of diplomatic engagement,” he told Bernama in a recent interview.
The ambassador noted that Sultan Ibrahim made history in August last year by becoming the first King of Malaysia to undertake a state visit to Russia since diplomatic relations were established in 1967.
His Majesty later returned to Russia in January this year for a special visit, during which the King toured the Hermitage Museum in St Petersburg with President Vladimir Putin.
According to Latypov, Russia was deeply honoured to welcome Sultan Ibrahim again in May this year for the Victory Day celebrations.
"Victory Day is very important for Russia. We pay tribute to those who sacrificed their lives for the freedom and independence of our country,” he said.
Latypov said that during Sultan Ibrahim’s Victory Day visit, His Majesty held talks with Russian President Putin, with both leaders reaching agreements.
"I believe the agreements will give fresh impetus to the development of Russia-Malaysia relations,” he added.
According to Sputnik and RIA Novosti, Sultan Ibrahim also invited President Putin to undertake a state visit to Malaysia in 2027 in conjunction with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic ties.
In early June, the Russian news agency TASS reported that Russia aims to abolish visa requirements for citizens of a few countries, including Malaysia.
Later in June, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim attended the ASEAN-Russia Commemorative Summit in Kazan, the capital and largest city of Tatarstan.
In his speech during a meeting with the Malaysian delegation led by Anwar, President Putin said that bilateral trade between Russia and Malaysia grew by 12.9 per cent last year.
"A very encouraging result,” he said, according to the speech transcript published on the Kremlin's website.
During the meeting, Russia also agreed to guarantee long-term supplies of petrol, oil and gas to Malaysia.
Geostrategist and senior fellow at the Nusantara Academy for Strategic Research (NASR), Prof Dr Azmi Hassan, when contacted by Bernama, said Sultan Ibrahim's royal diplomacy carries immense prestige that opens crucial "windows of opportunity” beyond the reach of conventional diplomatic channels.
"We can see that the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's first visit last August significantly expanded cooperation, not only at the diplomatic level but, more importantly, in the area of energy security. Malaysia has received assurances of long-term fuel supplies from Russia.
"Royal diplomacy plays a very critical role in strengthening diplomatic relations between the Prime Minister of Malaysia and the President of Russia,” he said.
Looking ahead to President Putin’s planned state visit to Malaysia in 2027, Azmi emphasised that Malaysia must look beyond traditional trade and prioritise acquiring advanced science and technology from Moscow.
"Russia has basically similar advancements and technology to Western nations. With Russia, we (Malaysia) can procure it at a more competitive cost. I think that is a more important thing and agenda that should be put on the table during Putin's visit next year,” he said.
In 2025, Russia was Malaysia’s ninth-largest trading partner among European nations, with total trade valued at RM8.72 billion (US$2.04 billion).
Malaysia’s main exports to Russia comprise electrical and electronic products, machinery, equipment and parts, as well as processed food products.
Its principal imports from Russia include petroleum products, minerals, chemicals and chemical-based products.
Diplomatic relations between the two nations were formally established on April 3, 1967, alongside the signing of a trade agreement.
Russia later opened its Trade Office in Kuala Lumpur in November 1967 and its embassy in April 1968, while Malaysia established its embassy in Moscow in November 1968. — Bernama

Title: Sabah Immigration denies viral claim of Filipino detainee deaths at depot
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, July 26 — The Sabah Immigration Department has denied a viral claim alleging that many Filipino detainees had died due to overcrowding at the state’s immigration detention depots.
State Immigration director Datuk SH Sitti Saleha Habib Yussof said that the allegation was false, baseless and misleading.
She also said the photograph circulating on social media was not taken at any Immigration detention depot in Sabah.
“All Filipino detainees housed at the Immigration detention depots in Sabah are in good condition while awaiting repatriation to their home country,” she said in a statement today.
She said that throughout their detention, all detainees are provided with appropriate care and protection in accordance with the law and the prevailing standard operating procedures.
Sitti Saleha said detainees are provided with basic necessities, including meals served according to a fixed schedule and in line with menus and nutritional standards approved by the Health Ministry to meet the needs of both adults and children.
She said detainees are also given access to medical treatment whenever necessary, as well as other essential needs.
Sitti Saleha said the repatriation of Filipino detainees via sea from Sandakan to Zamboanga, which had previously been the main repatriation route, has been suspended by the Philippine authorities since February, affecting the smooth implementation of the repatriation process.
“To ensure that repatriation continues, Sabah Immigration Department is using alternative routes, namely flights from Kota Kinabalu to Manila and sea transport from Lahad Datu to Bongao.
“However, repatriation through these alternative routes is subject to the detainees’ families agreeing to bear the travel costs,” she said.
She said the department remains committed to safeguarding the welfare, safety and health of all detainees while ensuring that the repatriation process is carried out in accordance with the law, established procedures and close cooperation with the Philippine authorities.
The public was also advised not to believe or spread unverified and misleading information, photographs or content, and to obtain accurate information through the Immigration Department’s official channels. — Bernama

Title: Former PM Muhyiddin says it should be PAS exiting Perikatan, not Bersatu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Bersatu president Muhyiddin Yassin has pushed back against calls for his party to leave Perikatan Nasional (PN), arguing that PAS — not Bersatu — should be the one to step away from the coalition after choosing to end political cooperation between the two parties.
FMT reported Muhyiddin saying said Bersatu, as a co‑founder of PN, could not be forced out of the coalition and retained every right to remain. “If a party decides to cut ties, it is usually the one that leaves the coalition,” he said, pointing to PAS’s past withdrawal from Pakatan Rakyat and Bersatu’s own exit from Pakatan Harapan.
Muhyiddin likened the situation to disagreements within a shared “house”, saying it was illogical to demand that Bersatu vacate the coalition when PAS was the party that initiated the split. He added that PAS appeared keen to hold on to PN’s value and was instead attempting to push Bersatu out.
PAS ended its cooperation with Bersatu early last month, though both remain PN components. The coalition, now chaired by PAS vice‑president Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, has since admitted two new members — Pejuang and Parti Wawasan Negara, led by former Bersatu deputy president Hamzah Zainudin.
Tensions between PAS and Bersatu have been visible on the ground. Although both parties contested under the PN banner in the July 11 Johor polls, PAS chose not to campaign for Bersatu, and the coalition was wiped out in the state. Ahead of the Aug 1 Negeri Sembilan election, PAS‑led PN struck a seat‑avoidance pact with Barisan Nasional, allocating 25 seats to BN and 11 to PN. Bersatu rejected the arrangement and opted to run under its own banner in 24 seats, creating eight direct clashes with PN.
Muhyiddin also reiterated that he intends to step down as Bersatu president when his term ends next year, saying the party needs renewal and fresh leadership. Although he previously announced he would not defend the presidency at the 2023 general assembly, he later stayed on after delegates urged him to continue for another term.

Title: Mohamad Hasan says non-Malays have ‘no reason to be unduly worried’ by BN-Perikatan pact in Negeri Sembilan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has assured non-Malay voters they will not be sidelined if the coalition secures victory in the upcoming Negeri Sembilan state election, despite its cooperation with Perikatan Nasional (PN).
According to
The Star
, BN deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said claims by rivals that minorities would be marginalised were unfounded, stressing that BN remained the dominant force in the partnership.
